text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link AC1900 Smart WiFi Router (Archer A8) -High Speed MU-MIMO Wireless Router, Dual Band Router for Wireless Internet, Gigabit, Supports Guest WiFi I wrote this review with a heavy dose of input from my husband, who is a retired IT professional.

We had a problem with the router supplied by our internet provider. It was causing all the devices on the network to lose their connection multiple times per day. The provider sent us a new router, but it was a "black box" device that did not allow for configuration by the user or even the provider's tech support personnel. So we decided to buy our own router. After quite a bit of research, we picked this one.

PROS

-Good speed at 600Mbps for the 2.4GHz band and 1300Mbps for the 5GHz band.
-It is configurable by the user. I can sign on to the admin page via my browser and change settings. The setting we most wanted to change was the default DHCP server lease time setting. For a home network such as ours that always has the same devices using it, there is no need to have short (i.e., hours long) DHCP lease time setting. The constant renewing of the lease can cause connection issues for the devices. At least, that has been our experience.
-The device seems very stable. Since swapping it in for the internet provider's router, we have had no dropping connections whatsoever. We are quite pleased with this router.
-2 year warranty.

CONS

-The maximum DHCP lease time setting was only a couple of days, unlike a previous router I had, which allowed you to go up to 30. But this is not really a big disadvantage. I have not noticed a problem with it.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC1900 Smart WiFi Router (Archer A8) -High Speed MU-MIMO Wireless Router, Dual Band Router for Wireless Internet, Gigabit, Supports Guest WiFi

text_fidelity_a: Michael Kors Access Gen 4 MKGO Smartwatch- Lightweight Touchscreen Powered with Wear OS by Google with Heart Rate, GPS, NFC, and Smartphone Notifications I have so many feelings about this watch. First off, set up was a breeze. You just open your app store and get the Google app directed. Pairing and synching up your info is very easy. The watch is very beautiful! I was scared the crystals would rub right off like glitter, but I have not had any issues so far. Now for all the bad stuff.. first and foremost the battery life is terrible. I would give it 9-10 hours max. I'm not much of an app person either, so if you are then that means your battery life will be even lower. It has its own charger, so that means you'll have to carry it around with you, especially big your planning to go out after work or school which is very inconvenient. I with it was a standard C USB charger so I can just use my phone charger, but sadly that's not the case. I did an experiment to see how long the battery would last. I charged it to 100%, and left it in my desk right before bed. In the morning at 8 am, I am at 15%. Whoa. Yeah, the battery is just really really terrible. So I thought I'd just change the battery settings..well there is only one other option and that is to go into battery saving mode where all it will display is the time. That in my opinion defeats the purpose of a smart watch. Other than that, I love how I can customize watch faces by using my social media, or pick from a pre made list by Michael Kors. You can also get email notifications, download apps like Google keep to take notes by speaking into your watch, as well as use Google pay, activity tracker, weather, and pause and play music without taking out your phone. So yeah, if your okay with a short battery life, then everything else about this watch is awesome. Just giving you the real tea. Hope you found this review helpful.
text_fidelity_b: Michael Kors Access Gen 4 MKGO Smartwatch- Lightweight Touchscreen Powered with Wear OS by Google with Heart Rate, GPS, NFC, and Smartphone Notifications

PANASONIC Wings Sport Headphones are Ultra-Light Wireless Bluetooth Sport Earbud 3D Flex Sport Clips with Microphone and Call/Volume Controller, IPX5 Rated Water-Resistant - RP-BTS35-K (Black) I received these earphones from Amazon Vine in early January, 2018. I liked the over-the-ears design. It makes the earphones far less likely to fall off when exercising. The sound quality is also excellent. I found its wireless bluetooth function quite handy for listening to music on my smartphone while walking, biking, lifting weights or doing calisthenics.

In short, as long as the battery could be charged, these sport earphones worked quite well. But suddenly, a few weeks ago, after only 7 months of use, the battery simply would no longer take a charge. The manual says that the battery should last through up to 300 charges, and there is absolutely no way that in only seven months I charged this device 300 times. It holds a charge well while the battery is working, much better than the other bluetooth earbuds that I have owned. So I could use it for up to five days without charging the battery. This means that, in seven months, I only charged the battery about 42-50 times, at most. This means the life of the battery was a mere 16% of what the manufacturer promised!

This is not a device in which the battery can be replaced. Therefore, once the battery dies, the earphones are worthless. Since the warranty is only for 90 days, there is no recourse with the manufacturer for replacing this device after that length of time.

The way that this product works is a good idea, but until the design includes the possibility of replacing the battery, the high price is simply not worth it. I will have to stick to cheap earbuds which are not such a hit to my pocketbook when their non-replaceable battery dies.

I rate this product as follows:

Sound quality 5 stars
Durability of battery: 1 star
Value for price: 1 star
Overall average: 2.3 stars
text_fidelity_b: PANASONIC Wings Sport Headphones are Ultra-Light Wireless Bluetooth Sport Earbud 3D Flex Sport Clips with Microphone and Call/Volume Controller, IPX5 Rated Water-Resistant - RP-BTS35-K (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
SanDisk SDSSDX-120G-G25 Extreme SSD 120GB SATA 6.0 Gb-s2.5-Inch Solid State Drive (SSD) A great product that works as described.

After flashing the SSD firmware from a bootable CD, putting a 120gb SanDisk Extreme in a (Dell GX620 sff/3ghz Pentium Dual Core w/2gb of RAM) was a walk in the park and so was installing Linux Mint 13 Cinnamon on the SSD. Enabling the Trim function as described on various Mint/Ubuntu websites went without a hitch. I've enabled a few other basic tweaks and they also have worked without any problems. Be sure to use the the EXT4 file system when partitioning, Linux Mint 13 uses it by default. Do not use the Linux Mint 13 KDE release, not even Orkin could kill all the bugs on that turkey.

At this point I am using the swap partition and browser caching on the SSD, but will be moving those to RAM as soon as Amazon gets my memory delivered to bump my computer up to 4gb. A note to other Dell GX620 owners. The Normal mode in the BIOS is in fact AHCI mode, as such it does fully support the Trim function. Linux can also emulate the Trim function using CRON if you do not have an AHCI capable box.

I'm telling you all this because getting the information to determine whether an SSD would work on my computer was like pulling teeth. User Name "SpeedStep" on the Dell forums was a lot of help.

Buy an SSD, you'll like it. Unless your Mac or an XP user, it isn't that big a deal.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk SDSSDX-120G-G25 Extreme SSD 120GB SATA 6.0 Gb-s2.5-Inch Solid State Drive (SSD)

text_fidelity_a:
Dolica GX600B200 Proline GX Series 60-Inch Aluminum Tripod and Ball Head Combo for DSLR This review is for the Dolica GX600B200 Proline GX Series 60-Inch Aluminum Tripod and Ball Head Combo for DSLR.

The pros:
-Light weight for a full-sized 60-inch tripod, especially for one made of aluminum.
-Unlike some other reviewers, I really like the carrying bag. The tripod fits just fine as long as the legs are telescoped fully, and the bag seems like it is well made. It has a zippered pocket on the inside with two spare hex keys.
-Pan function is very smooth. I don't shoot video often, but I can see that this feature will be very nice for those times when I do.
-Textured rubber feet grip well, and there are metal spikes which can be revealed if needed for extra grip on ice.
-Quick-release plate is metal instead of plastic. It also can be adjusted from side to side so that it can conform to a battery hatch on the bottom of a DSLR.

Cons:
-My biggest complaint is that there is no handle to maneuver the ball head. This makes it very difficult to make fine adjustments. A removable handle, or any sort of handle for that matter, would be a massive improvement for this tripod.
-The bubble level is on the body of the tripod. It should be on the ball head where it might actually be useful.
-The release locks on the legs are absurdly stiff to open. This makes it more difficult to extend them quickly, and also makes the tripod a very poor choice for anyone with arthritic hands. I believe it will also make it quite difficult to use in cold weather with cold, stiff fingers.
-The central column is very wobbly when fully extended, and the thumb screw used to stabilize it is totally insufficient for the task.
- Edited to add: after use in the field I found that the tripod maintains a certain amount of wobble for a few seconds after handling it, or in a breeze. It's not terribly sturdy compared to similar tripods.

Overall thoughts:
This tripod seems like a good compromise for weight and price. If I wanted a lighter tripod of higher quality I would have to spend a lot more money and get a carbon fiber tripod. I do regret the lack of a handle on the ball head. While it is not terribly sturdy, and I would not rely on this tripod extended to full height with heavy glass on the camera, for casual use it seems like it will work just fine.
text_fidelity_b: Dolica GX600B200 Proline GX Series 60-Inch Aluminum Tripod and Ball Head Combo for DSLR

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Wireless Reading Device (6" Display, U.S. Wireless) I am probably one of the least intuitive people around when it comes to technology. I've bought quite a few gadgets that have ended up collecting dust as I never really learned to use them properly. My short lived relationship with a Palm Pilot ended in frustration when I didn't learn how to back it up on my PC and all my carefully inputted data was lost (more than once!) My kids use it now for a doodle pad. My husband says I have a "black thumb" when it comes to anything electronic. If there is a way to break it, lose it, or misuse it, I'm right there doing it. This is why it is so astonishing that I have grown to love my kindle 2.

I learned how to use it easily within a few minutes. It is so intuitive- my four year old enjoys it and can page back and forth reading classics such as George MacDonald's The Princess and The Goblin or Mary Pope Osborne's The Magic Treehouse. My tween age son uses it for Shakespeare- I downloaded the First Folio (35 plays from the Bard) for all of 99 cents! It's quite a favorite amongst my children and I have recently learned that if more than one family member has a kindle, all e-books may be shared with a single purchase. My friend can even access her kindle books and magazines from her iphone!

Cool features include 6 different options for font size, and text markers by "location" to bring you to the same line of text whether you use the biggest or smallest of fonts, as page numbers would vary too much to be useful. A male or female voice can read to you, though the voices are a bit stiff and robotic, and they make small mistakes such as using alternate pronunciation that don't fit context with heteronyms such as read/read or live/live. You can connect speakers or earbuds/headphones for this feature. Magazines can be downloaded as a single issue or a subscription, but the subscriptions cannot be canceled from the kindle- the user must go to amazon's "Manage my kindle" area to do this.

I have downloaded quite a few classic books for free and spent about a dollar on many others. So far, the younger children's literature has been somewhat limited, but I imagine that as prices drop, more will become available. I am a bibliophile and I never thought I would love a paper book replacement, but this device is so clean and glare free that I forget I am not looking at a paper page.

I'm sure that color kindles will be available within a few years, to make the illustrations a bit more interesting. I love the beautiful pen and ink type renderings which fill the kindle 2 screen when it isn't in use. Obviously though, color would be more attractive with other types of art. Black and white is easiest on the eyes for text, and mostly that it what kindle is all about.

The kindle 2 holds a charge for a long time. I think I plug mine in about once every couple of weeks. If you are not careful with the five way button, sometimes you do end up getting the wrong result. I purchased a book accidentally this way, but amazon has a handy "did you purchase this by mistake?" option which permits you to cancel the order if you act right away.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Wireless Reading Device (6" Display, U.S. Wireless)

text_fidelity_a:
Arlo VMS5140-100NAS Ultra - 4K UHD Wire-Free Security 1 Camera System Update: one star. Stopped holding a charge after 3 months.

These are the first security cameras we've ever used, and I was able to install them myself in about a half hour. While they do a good job recording video and saving it so I can view it on my phone, the app is lacking and there are a couple of things that I find frustrating. I'll break my review into pros and cons.

Pros:
1. Fast install
2. Rechargeable (but only one base station)
3. Can view what is going on in my house when I am not there, can talk to the dog if I see him getting into the trash
4. Backs up my videos so I can look at them later if I am not home but cannot check the notification
5. I like the option to have a light come on at night, sound a siren, or call emergency services.
6. Decent video, I don't think it's 4k HD though, and wonderful audio.

Cons
1. The battery life. It lasts about 5 days, but one of mine is mounted outside so I have to stand on a chair or ladder to disconnect it and reconnect it.
2. Only one charing base is included for two cameras. They usually die around the same time and I can only charge one, the extra chargers are pricey and it seems to be a proprietary wire.
3. It came with one magnetic mount, which I love, and another mount that is a screw and ball. This mount doesn't feel as secure and I don't get why it just didn't have two of the same ones. It looks weird having the same camera with different mounts.
3. They are 4k, IF you pay. If you don't then they record in a lower quality. I don't mind, but it's misleading how it's phrased.
4. The app is clunky. I found it hard to block out areas where I didn't need notifications (like, every car that drives by on the road). I also was overwhelmed with notifications every time someone walks through my living room. I figured out how to set the cameras to a schedule/geo-fence, but WATCH OUT! The geo-fence doesn't work if you disconnect your phone from Wifi when you leave.
5. Notifications: When I'm not home I get an alert every time my cats walk through the room, so I had to shut off notifications all together. A little frustrating, but understandable.
6. Timers. If you want the camera to run from 10pm to 5am, you have to set it for the current day 10pm-11:59 pm, then the next day from 12:01am to 5:00am. It's kind of difficult and it kept not saving it when I set it up that way so I gave up and just set it from 12:01am-5:00am.
text_fidelity_b: Arlo VMS5140-100NAS Ultra - 4K UHD Wire-Free Security 1 Camera System

text_fidelity_a:
Nitecore SC2 Superb Charger 3A Quick Charge Bundle with EASTSHINE EB182 Battery Organizer Overall, this is a solid charger. The build quality is top-notch, it’s sized so that you don’t have to struggle to put in/take out 26650s, and the 3A charge rate is a treat. However, it has a design issue that, while not a major roadblock, can be quite irritating.

Let’s start with the good news. This is one solidly-built charger. Compared with other chargers in its general price class from Efest and Xtar, this has a lot more heft to it. The sliders are perfect – not too loose; not too tight – and move smoothly without any crunchiness or squeaking. Best of all, it can hold two 26650s without any difficulty getting them in or out of the slots. That’s a great feature since I’ve been using a lot more 26650 mods recently, and getting those fat batteries in or out of some of my Xtar chargers is a major pain.

Other ease of use features include non-slip feet on the base that keep it firmly planted. The included power cord does not have a wall wart on the end – just a regular plug – which is a welcome change. All in all I have absolutely zero complaints about the fit and finish.

Performance is also solid. Each slot is independent, and can be set to charge at up to 3A. However, only one channel can be set at 3A since the total cannot exceed 5A. But even one 3A channel is a great feature if you use large capacity 26650s that can support a 3A input. It cuts the recharge time to the bone. It also has a USB output for charging (2.1A). However, you must leave slot 2 empty if you want the USB charging to take priority. Otherwise, it will charge the cell in slot 2 first, then charge via USB.

The charger has all the customary protection features that you would expect from a good quality charger such as overtime protection, reverse polarity protection, and auto shut off if it runs more than 10 hours. It also has a recovery mode for deeply discharged Li-ion cells. I never use that (if I accidently deeply discharge a cell I no longer use it) but it has the feature should it be of value for your needs. Heat output when running was very low.

The current for each slot can be set to 0.5A, 1A, 2A or 3A. You can also set the cutoff voltage to 1.2v, 3.7v, 4.2v or 4.3v. I use this nearly only with Li-ion cells, so the 4.2v cutoff is what I use for most of my charging. However, it’s nice to have the 3.7v setting for when I want to charge cells for long-term storage.

If you do nothing, the charger will set itself to a 2A current for cells that are greater than 1200mAh, and 0.5A for cells less than 1200mAh. You can override the settings for both current and cutoff independently for each channel.

And that’s where the biggest irritation occurs. The charger has a double row of LED lights that signify current and cutoff levels (plus blink to show operation, and stop blinking when charging is done). Simple and unobtrusive. However, there are no notations on the screen to show what charge rate/cutoff corresponds to each LED. Instead, those numbers are listed on a piece of clear plastic that is stuck on top of the display. It peels off easily and looks like a temporary cover to protect the screen.

In addition to looking poor, the lack of durability of the cover with the numbers listed means it won’t survive for long. Now, there are only four positions for the LEDs so it’s not a huge puzzler to decipher the settings if you use the charger regularly. However, I have several chargers and can go a couple of weeks between using one in particular. It can be hard to remember which LED position means what. And I shouldn’t have to do that – numbers should be imprinted right on the screen and not on a flimsy piece of plastic.

I also don’t care for the fact that the button labels (one for current, one for cutoff) are embossed into the plastic. The black-on-black makes it very hard to see which button is which.

But those issues aside, this is a solid charger that offers up to 3A charging. The build quality and operation are both excellent, and it’s perfectly sized to hold two 26650 cells without a bit of struggle to get them in or out of the slots. The poorly designed screen and button labels drops my score to 4.5 stars, but I’ll round up since everything else is well executed.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Nitecore SC2 Superb Charger 3A Quick Charge Bundle with EASTSHINE EB182 Battery Organizer

AMD FD8350FRHKBOX FX-8350 FX-Series 8-Core Black Edition Processor Immediately after installing I noticed the idle speed just sitting in BIOS to be 50C. That's quite a bit! More than any processor I've come across.
At first I thought I seated it wrong so I undid the heat sink, used really good thermal paste and tried once more.
Same result. Idle temp at 50C.
And under load it's getting up to into the low 60s and termal throttling like crazy. However it seems to perform well even under that heavy load, which is nice if that's all you care about.
But I'm doing a build for my dad and I don't think he'd be content with having to hear a jet engine under his desk day in and day out. So I'm going to have to look elsewhere.
That's on me though. I probably should have known better from my experience with another FX processor. Ah well.
Still considering if I'm returning this or not.

UPDATE:
Ok, I did some more digging and it sounds like my motherboard is not equipped to handle this processor.
WARNING: If you have a MSI 970A-G46 Motherboard DO NOT BUY THIS PROCESSOR.
Go research "MSI 970A-G46 FX 8350"
You'll find numerous testimonials of people who have had terminal issues trying to use a FX 8350 with this board.
Since the MB is at fault for this and I can not accurately benchmark this product, I'll give AMD the benefit of the doubt and make this 5 stars.
text_fidelity_b: AMD FD8350FRHKBOX FX-8350 FX-Series 8-Core Black Edition Processor

Panasonic HomeHawk Outdoor Wireless Smart Home Security Camera, Wide Angle View, Color Night Vision, 2-Way Talk, Works with Alexa & Google Assistant, 1 Camera Kit (KX-HN7001W) The Panasonic HomeHawk system has its good and its areas that could use some upgrades.
The good:
This is about as simple and install as you will get for a home monitoring system. No wires, five screws, charging the camera, downloading the app and you are ready to go, it is that simple. Once the cameras are charged and mounted I think it took me about 5 minutes to get everything running, and I am not technical by any stretch of the imagination.
The cameras are clear and provide good picture (you can select the quality of the picture when setting the system up) of the areas they are monitoring. Recordings are of good quality and clear, the night recording can be either color or black and white (infrared) depending on your choice.
Recording trigger areas can be set up along with sensitivity to movement in the recording area to trigger the recording to begin. All of these are very handy and easy to use.
The app is simple to use and pretty intuitive on how the system operates allowing almost everyone to use the system without any special knowledge. In all a good system for 95% of the people out there.
The things that can be improved.
It became apparent during setup of the outdoor camera (the one that looks like ET) that you need to mount it in a specific orientation, if you turn it over you cannot flip the image and everything will be upside down. If the ball neck for mounting the camera was just a little longer this would not be an issue as you could fit it under a soffit on your house wit a large field of view.
On the outdoor camera it works best when the rear of the camera is pointed in the direction of the base unit for connectivity. As you turn the camera and point the rear away from the base the signal drops pretty quick and the camera will not connect.
Other than these items the system is pretty easy to set up and use, now we see all the raccoons that show up to the house at night.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic HomeHawk Outdoor Wireless Smart Home Security Camera, Wide Angle View, Color Night Vision, 2-Way Talk, Works with Alexa & Google Assistant, 1 Camera Kit (KX-HN7001W)

TP-Link AC3200 Wireless Wi-Fi Tri-Band Gigabit Router (Archer C3200) The router is amazing... Great speeds and looks visually appealing in a room. It has enough processing power that it is able to route data to many wired and wireless device simultaneously and not have any slow downs and the 6 flip out antennas allow the device to have plenty of range to reach even the far corners of the house.

The 3 bands of wireless signal are great, it consists of 1, 2.4ghz network, and 2, 5ghz networks, so that you can assign wireless traffic it's own separate band in order to prevent congestion of a single band.
Remember that a 2.4ghz band will reach further but will be slower, while a 5ghz band will be significantly faster while not reaching as far.

For the more advanced people out there, there are plenty of options that you would expect from a mid range router like this, custom DNS servers, MAC address blocking, port forwarding, DHCP fine tuning, and it also allows you to plug in a USB flash drive into the USB port to use as a small NAS.

The user interface is also quite nice, it is visually appealing and very modern, while retaining functionality and still having the advanced features available for the people who need it.

text_fidelity_a:
10 Inch Tablet, 64GB Storage Tablets, Android 11 Tab, 512GB Expandable, 8MP+2MP Camera, 1.5Ghz CPU Quad-Core Processor, 2GB RAM WiFi 6000mAh Battery, 10.1'' HD 1280*800 IPS Touch Screen Google Tablet I was one of the FIRST people to own an iPad back when they were introduced. It was a birthday gift. And, I honestly regret giving up a trip to Disneyland for it. Yes, I had a choice between what I thought was going to be a lifelong, productive item for a trip to Disneyland.

I did go to Disneyland in 2015 though, so I was a few years late. Regrets? Should’ve taken the trip and NOT gotten the iPad. It barely works today (can’t upgrade the iOS due to NOT having a camera – a front facing one for some updates). And, I have it in my desk drawer. REALLY PEEVED at Apple for that one.

So, I’ve been REAL hesitant to jump on the eReader or tablet train. They upgrade, change, and modify so fast. Honestly, I use my iPhone for certain things while I use my laptop. The rest? I use my laptop. I don’t really read eBooks to justify an eReader, nor do I like it. [I did try it with this – still a no go – clunky, awkward, no “book smell”, and so easy to lose my place.]

Seeing this? I decided to grab it. After all, I USED to be a Samsung Galaxy (Android) user. I had to replace my GS8 and the iPhone I was had a cheaper plan through my carrier. No regrets there. But, I still remember the Android system. My mom still has her GS8 phone, so I HAVE to know it.

Looking at the price, around $60 (as of this review) – this is a basic, no frills tablet. It is a “no-name” brand, but that doesn’t mean much. I’ve had trouble with numerous brand name items, so name doesn’t matter.

Now, this is VERY SLOW. Even a cheap Acer laptop can be slow. My mom had one and the language … hello? Content warning!!

This is, to me, great for pre-teens and teens. It’s not too expensive that parents will really scream if something happens (like say an iPad or more expensive $100+ tablet). Or, it can work for someone who wants some internet functionality, and wants to read eBooks. The Kindle app works great here, just not my style.

I can check my email accounts – Outlook and Gmail – no real issues. I’ve ordered fast-food. As far as games? The one I tried didn’t work (Hogwarts Mystery)

As far as a user manual – like most devices nowadays (or the ones I’ve bought in the last 5-8 years) – the MANUAL (instructions) are on the device, usually a PDF. This was the same for the last three HP laptops I bought in 2010, 2011, and 2019. And, it was the same for the last two phones (GS8 and iPhone 11). Also, my iPods in 2008 and 2013. So, yes, I do have a LOT of experience with the lack of a physical manual. The manual can be accessed by swiping the homescreen UP. It is a PDF file.

There are some apps that ARE NOT COMPATIBLE with this device, even if you have them on a Galaxy phone. These can range from productivity to fast food. IE: Tropical Smoothie Café’s app is compatible, Taco Bell isn’t. My bank’s app isn’t compatible, but I can access the website through the Chrome browser (which I also have on my iPhone).

However, a GIANT bonus for me – MICROSOFT 365. I was able to add WORD to the tablet, and since I have cloud storage – ALL MY DOCUMENTS are AVAILABLE to view and edit.

Overall – this is, as I stated: a BASIC or STARTER tablet. Better suited for ages 8 to 15. I say this based on the fact that at 8, I would be able to care for this, and use it. By 15, I’d likely save up my allowance for a higher priced tablet or get it as a gift.

I am pretty pleased with it, and will likely use it for several things.
text_fidelity_b: 10 Inch Tablet, 64GB Storage Tablets, Android 11 Tab, 512GB Expandable, 8MP+2MP Camera, 1.5Ghz CPU Quad-Core Processor, 2GB RAM WiFi 6000mAh Battery, 10.1'' HD 1280*800 IPS Touch Screen Google Tablet

text_fidelity_a:
Patriot Memory Supersonic Boost XT USB 3.0 8GB Flash Drive (PEF8GSBUSB) While I do most of my work at the office, there are times that I want, or need, to work on certain things at home. This was the easiest and most cost effective way to be able to transport documents home and back to work again. I ordered this particular flash drive becasue not only did it have a key ring attachment, it also appeared to be pretty rugged and well protected. Many others leave the USB port open/exposed and that just felt a little risky since I knew I would be carrying it back and forth every day. Upon opening it, I liked it! It is not as small and flashy as many others but for my purposes it was perfect. It felt very durable and I wasn't worried about carrying it around with me all the time. I put it on my work key ring and have enjoyed the convenience of having it. I especially like this drive because there is no software to download or set-up required. I just plug it in and go to work.
I loved it until a couple of days ago when I pulled the cap off only to find I had pulled the entire unit out of the protective case. I was worried about the USB being exposed and now the whole flash drive chip was exposed! There is a small clear plastic piece that nests just inside the lip of the rubberized case that keeps the unit in place inside the casing. When I tried to pull the cap off, which is a bit snug, it pulled the entire unit out, dislodging the small plastic piece. I have tried to slide it back into place, but to no avail, so there is no longer anything holding the "guts" of the drive inside the casing. I was not being too rough on it and have intentionally tried to gently remove the cap every time I use it. From such a rugged, solid first appearance, I am very dissapointed that this happened just a little over a month after receiving it, So far, I have still been able to retrieve my data off the device so I have not lost anything there. And luckily I ordered this from Amazon, a company that is fairly easy to work with. They will be providing a replacement so all I am out is the effort to transfer the data over to the new unit. I hope the next one will hold up because I really did like it and I would like to be able to enter another review letting you know that this one was just a fluke. We'll see!
text_fidelity_b: Patriot Memory Supersonic Boost XT USB 3.0 8GB Flash Drive (PEF8GSBUSB)

text_fidelity_a:
KINESIS Freestyle2 USB Keyboard for Mac (9" Standard Separation), Black Overall this keyboard is great. The keys feel nice and they're quiet but not too quiet or soft or squishy. Enjoy typing on this keyboard, pushing the keys seems to take minimal effort and overall it's great.

The best part about the keyboard is that it separates and having the ability to give it a little separation is great. I miss it when I don't have it and it helps avoid torquing the wrists when you are typing. I also love the feel of the keys.

Now before my minor complaints understand two things: (1) I really like this keyboard and despite what I would consider minor defects, I would definitely buy another one. (2) please excuse the fact that I like my keyboards to be consistent and while Apple may not make the *best* keyboards I do use a laptop and I am used to their keyboard layout and feel.

The biggest thing that annoyed me when I purchased this keyboard was the positioning of the ⌘ (command) key. It seems to be shifted over a bit from what I'm used to. Normally I would hit ⌘ with my thumb but it's a little touch to do that on this one given the position of it. It's just something I'm having to get used to.

One minor downside to the keyboard is that the function key doesn't work the same way as the default apple keyboard, rather, the `fn` key is a toggle. I prefer for fn to work as a modifier because that is what I am used to on my laptop keyboard.

Another minor problem is the styling on the caps lock key. Like many people, I remap my caps lock to ctrl and and thus want caps lock to be a normal button. However, on this keyboard the caps lock key is missing the right part of the key so that you don't accidentally hit it when typing the `a` key.

Finally, the escape key and '`' (back tick) keys are in weird positions. The escape key is not as bad as the backtick. There is just something about the distance that I must go that is different from what I'm used to and I have been consistently hitting the `1` key instead. Life goes on.
text_fidelity_b: KINESIS Freestyle2 USB Keyboard for Mac (9" Standard Separation), Black

text_fidelity_a:
Bose SoundTouch 10 wireless speaker, works with Alexa - Black Before writing this review I glanced over some reviews of earlier models, and whatever issues previous editions of the Bose SoundTouch speakers may have had seem to have been worked out with this SoundTouch 10.

Setup was simple with the SoundTouch app (available for iOS, Android, and Kindle Fire devices). We had the speaker set up and operating in less than 5 minutes using an iPad. You'll need your home network security code to connect to WiFi and that's about it.

It comes with a remote, but most of the controlling is done from your device (tablet or phone). The remote is handy for adjusting the volume when you're using your device for other things.

The speaker is about the size of a cereal box. The sound that comes out is impressive for its size. I think there's a wee bit of case resonance in the mid range, but that's just me -- everyone else thinks it sounds terrific. It doesn't rival a huge stereo system but it's really, really good.

Now excuse me while I get on my soapbox about monaural. This is a single speaker system, not stereo, and that, to me, is a good thing. I'm a fan of monaural. It solves a lot of issues about speaker placement (trying to make sure they're equally distant), and you hear the full mix as the producers and artists intended. You can move anywhere around the room and not have half the mix disappear. And if you like oldies, particularly from the 1960s, this fixes the problems caused by common pan/mix practices from that era (for example, drums and bass panned hard left, guitars and backup singers panned hard right, lead vocals in the middle). If you listen to mixes like that in headphones, you pretty much have to mix the music down in your imagination since bass/drums are exclusively in one ear and keyboards in the other. Some devices don't support mono audio output (I'm looking at you, Windows phone), and as far as I know no one makes a dual-ear mono headset for phones either. So a mono speaker solves the issue. Okay, that's it for the soapbox. Back to the review.

The only tone control available in the Bose app is bass volume. But since the sound is well engineered, it's adequate. And bass is very audible. Not subwoofer level audible, but it's very present.

The SoundTouch app itself is impressive. It really does make setup a breeze. And the listening options are VAST. Hundreds of radio stations from around the world on WiFi, streaming music services, Pandora, Spotify, and so forth. I used to do a little shortwave listening, and if you're a DXer, this exceeds the capability of SW by far, and every station is digitally clear. And you can connect directly to play music straight from your device.

Just to be clear, the speaker itself needs a wall outlet to power it. It's not battery powered. But everything else is wireless. More speakers can be added, but it's so easily unplugged and moved around that one speaker can easily be sufficient.

Nice product from Bose.
text_fidelity_b: Bose SoundTouch 10 wireless speaker, works with Alexa - Black

text_fidelity_a:
SABRE Home Security Personal Safety Kit, Comes With A 120 dB Doorstop Alarm, 120 dB Door Or Window Alarm And A 120 dB Personal Alarm, Safety Essentials For College Students, Home Owners and Travelers With crime rates going up in NYC, this is an ideal kit for anyone living in an apartment, especially if they're alone and elderly. It covers two areas most vulnerable to thieves: your window and the door, while the key chain is best for when you're coming home late at night on a dark, lonely street. Just pull the pin and the alarm screams.

Of the three items, I would say the window alarm rates highest in terms of usefulness. In fact, I wish this set came with three of them. We travel a lot, and the biggest fear we have is intruders breaking in through our high-rise window, as we have a fire escape near one of them.

The door stop is the least useful to me as a thief would have to break through one of our windows first before going through a door. My front door is already secured by locks and the other doors in our place generally remain open. I suppose we could reinforce the front door with the doorstop, but it seems like overkill. If you lived in a dorm and wanted a particular room to be off-limits, I suppose it would be useful in that case. This item reminds me of the alarm that would be set off if you used an emergency exit. As if in acknowledgement that this item won't be used as much as the others, no battery was supplied for it, unlike the others.

As for the key chain, this is one of those devices that will lay dormant for long periods (knock on wood). You'll have to remember to check and test the batteries occasionally because it will be rarely used.

Overall, for the price this set can't be beat. It feels more like a "sampler" pack, though, as it has only one of each product when multiples of each one would have been more helpful.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Home Security Personal Safety Kit, Comes With A 120 dB Doorstop Alarm, 120 dB Door Or Window Alarm And A 120 dB Personal Alarm, Safety Essentials For College Students, Home Owners and Travelers

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony Ultimate All in One Remote - Discontinued by Manufacturer Okay. At first I was not impressed with the Harmony Ultimate. After getting the system up and going, however, I love it.

Desired goal: control two entertainment systems in two rooms with four remotes -- two in each room.

3/29/16 update: I thought having a single remote talking to a single hub was a drawback. But the app on my iPhone is so effective, it's really a second remote for no extra cost. I don't even touch the actual remote that came with the system. That's for the wife, who has taken to the system easily and understands how to work it. I now love my system. Five stars.

3/17/16 Logitech Ultimate Remote w/Hub
Cons:
1. Only one remote can be paired with each hub. Want the wife to have her own remote on one side of the room and you to have another, both controlling the same equipment? Forget it. You can't.
2. Two hubs cannot talk to each other. So you buy two remotes and two hubs, thinking they will talk to each other over WiFi? Forget it. They can't.
3. Pricey at list. Acceptable when on sale ($120 off is nice)

Pros:
1. Excellent phone app. You do all programming from the phone after you create a Logitech cloud account. This gives you control of your system if your phone can reach the internet.
2. Excellent desktop app. Logitech has given up trying to use browsers; you use genuine local apps on your phone and laptop.
3. Easy to set up: Enter MFG and Model number for each device. Done. Full remote buttons download for each device.
4. Touch screen on both the remote and the app has "gestures" with one- or two-finger swiping to control devices. This is nice and unexpected.
5. Colorful
6. Recharges in the cradle -- no more AAA batteries!
7. Wakes up when you pick it up
8. Backlit buttons
9. Haptic feedback when a virtual button is pressed
10. Phone app is great for setup and works as a second remote.

Setting up the first remote was wonderful and very exciting. I couldn't wait to expand the system with my second hub and its remote to create a really capable, flexible system. When the second hub failed to talk to the first hub and I discovered that I had purchased two systems that cannot talk to each other, my elation went to mild disappointment.

Sequence to set up:

1. Create an account with Logitech Harmony at myharmony.com
2. Download the Harmony phone app and download the desktop exe to your laptop.
3. Log in to the account
4. Name and connect the first hub with you WiFi router password
5. Add devices to the room's hub by entering the Manufacturer and the Model number for each device
a. These devices can be far more than AV devices, including lights, blinds, thermostats and other things to a limit of 15.
b. Each device can be renamed for accurate familiarity
6. Create "Activities" for the devices you want to control:
I.e., "Blu-ray Living Rm"
a. it will ask first, "what devices are involved in this activity?"
b. checkbox "AV receiver Living Rm," "TV Living Rm," and "Blu-ray Living Rm"
c. the app asks, "Which input for the TV?" and "Which input for the AV Receiver?" and "Which device controls the volume?"
d. click "run test" to see if everything shuts off and turns back on correctly
e. if it's good, click "yes." Good to go to create next activity.

After you get one room's devices entered and working, if you have a second hub and remote, program it separately in the next room. You can rename the hubs using the desktop exe, but not from the phone app. This is very helpful if you are using the phone as a second remote. You'll have to switch hubs on the phone if you go from one room to another.

You can reorder the activities on both the phone and the remote for most logical order for that room
You can edit buttons and gestures and more.
You can add delay time if a unit needs more time to warm up before it can receive a command
You can change the timeout for the remote to go into standby
You can use your phone as a fully functional remote, but you do have to select which hub you want to talk to.
The Hub connects wirelessly to your WiFi router. It also acts as a giant IR blaster to send commands to the devices. It also has two 2.5mm mono sub-mini plug sockets and two "mini blaster" IR emitters that plug into these sockets so you can send IR to other places.

If you have a device in another room that needs to be controlled, you can extend one of the mini-blasters using an inexpensive 2.5mm extension cord like the 5-meter [[ASIN:B003OSR5TE kenable 2.5mm Stereo Jack Plug to 2.5mm Jack Socket Extension Cable 5m (~16.5 feet)]] or a wireless remote IR extension system like the [[ASIN:B0087S9CJ2 Monoprice 109194 Wireless Dual Band IR Remote Control Extender Upto 328-Feet]].

This wired or wireless extension to another room would be moot if the hubs talked to each other.

What Logitech needs to make happen is to allow multiple remotes to talk to multiple hubs and for the hubs to talk to each other. They've been promising this added capability since at least 2013 on their forums, but so far, it's one remote to one hub and workarounds.

Logitech should not market this as "Ultimate." It's very capable, but also not quite as flexible as required.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony Ultimate All in One Remote - Discontinued by Manufacturer

Defender HD1T4 HD 1080p 4 Channel 1TB Security DVR with Mobile Viewing, Black We couldn't find a way to set this up because of logistics, which is unfortunate. Wireless or Bluetooth options would have worked better for this, not only because of distances, but because having to work with wires at such lengths and hide them in a home would have been beyond unwieldy.

Problem 1: drilling from the exterior of the house to the inside in Florida, unless done by a professional, likely means you created a place for water and moisture to leak in, which inevitably means mold and other issues. Even so, it's understandable that this may be necessary pretty much every time, and perhaps that wouldn't be such a big deal if it weren't for problem 2.

Problem 2: for this to work, you need to have a tv or monitor setup. If you have a bigger space, the distance might be further to get from where you want to record to the place where you have those things.

Here's what would have worked to let us set this up:
Have a hub of some sort that can be put anywhere nearish to the cameras, and then that can connect wirelessly to an app, computer, or monitor on the same network, not just for setup, but in general.

We would have had to go from the garage area to the inside part of the house, somewhere over 70 feet? To get to the nearest tv or monitor.

I'll try again for my small business if we ever change locations, but having to attach to a monitor is a pain. It should be able to work directly from the hub/DVR to an app.
text_fidelity_b: Defender HD1T4 HD 1080p 4 Channel 1TB Security DVR with Mobile Viewing, Black

Arlo Pro - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Siren | Rechargeable, Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, 2-Way Audio, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 1 camera kit (VMS4130) After initial euphoria, I have to say that the ROI is marginal at best. Briefly, here is why:

Positive:
1. Excellent day and night picture quality
2. Simple configuration and UI.
3. Free storage up to limit.
4. Rugged construction
5. Integration with Smarthings and other IoT.
6. Easy setup. Ensure you buy the condoms and mounting brackets for outside.

Negative: (Relative to price point)
1. Battery life is marginal. If you never have motion in an area great. But, think about that front yard where you have people walking by or cars parked just on the edge of your property. With roughly 10-15 activation per day, the battery drains quickly. I feel I would be better off with a perm. powered device.
2. While it has a standard micro usb port similar to virtually any android smart phone. You still require the Arlo plug to charge. Not a deal breaker, but painful.
2. App load times/camera viewing is slow. I have a 100 mb Xfinity internet connection with Netgear Orbi Mesh setup within 15 ft of the front camera. Connection in my house is not the issue. I have a Samsung S7 device. Be prepared to wait upwards of 30 seconds before authentication, app loads AND THEN the camera activates to see who is at the front door. It needs to be faster.
3. The absolute worst aspect of the camera is that recording does not start fast enough. Roughly 30 seconds of an event (or more) go by before capture begins. This is not acceptable. I have tried playing with various settings but unable to resolve.

Overall, I regret purchasing now. I should have invested the time and installed a fixed camera setup.

12-Jul-17 - I have lowered the stars on this product because of the incredibly poor support provided for both this product and in particular the ORBI which I also have. The warranty on both products which are similarly priced make zero sense. Stay away from NETGEAR until they get their act together.

17-Aug-17 - Finally heard back from NETGEAR and received confirmation in their user forums that the original screw adapter on the VMA1000 mount for the solar panel is too big. (gee thanks..I knew that) I was sent new screws that now allow the solar cable to be plugged in along with the VMA1000 mount. Why these are not highlighted everywhere and why there is no update to the Amazon listing as a bulletin or something to look for when buying the solar panel, I don't know. Overall, I would say NETGEAR is completely lost on any form of cohesive support and sincerely hope my product continues to work as I do not want to ever have to call or email again..

June 2020
I am done with Arlo. The product is over-priced and unreliable. Here is why:
I added the doorbells 2 yes ago and 2 of 2 have been rma'd.
2 of the cameras have been rma'd.
1 of the 2 solar panels has apparently died as not properly charging. This after less than 2 years.
I only realized recently that some Einstein at Arlo decided to have the wifi channel operate on the exact channel my mesh is on. There are clearly issues.
The camera has good and bad days from an access perspective. Some days they come up in about 30 seconds. Some they don't load..
The delay of 5 seconds before motion activates recording is brutal. You can completely someone moving fast.
Arlo support has become poor after being fantastic initially.

This product will be going the way of my Orbi soon. I am done with Netgear ( or formerly Netgear) products...

Cable Matters DisplayPort to DVI Adapter (DP to DVI Adapter) My desktop computer has a built in graphics card on the motherboard and I added a graphics card for gaming. The graphics card has a DVI, VGA and DisplayPort outputs. I had two monitors hooked up, one to the DVI, and one to the VGA port. I had another monitor (actually a TV) which duplicated screen two using a splitter. But I wanted to use it as a third separate monitor.

I tried several things to make a third monitor work: a DVI to HDMI cable (not an active cable) didn't work - the computer never saw the third monitor. I also tried the built in graphics card on the motherboard, plugging in an HDMI cable to its port and connecting the TV. That didn't work. it seems only one graphics card can be enabled at a time; either the one on the motherboard, or the installed graphics card.

This worked. As soon as I plugged it in, going from the displayport on the graphics card to the HDMI cable, the computer saw & recognized the 3rd monitor. Now I have three separate monitors.

text_fidelity_a:
Linksys WiFi Extender, WiFi 6 Range Booster, Dual-Band Booster, Internet Repeater, 2,000 Sq. ft Coverage, Speeds up to (AX1800) 1.8Gbps - RE7310 You should know up front that this extender only works wirelessly with dual-band WiFi routers (routers with both 2.4GHz and 5GHz).

But it will work as a hard-wired range extender for single-band routers (2.4GHz) using an ethernet cable.

If you have a single band router like we do, it will not detect the wireless network or connect wirelessly. If our neighborhood is any indication, this extender won't work with most home routers. Out of the ten or so visible wireless networks in our area, the extender only detected one or two. The two it detected were two of the weaker signals, but I assume were dual band signals the extender would work with.

After several frustrating attempts to get it connected wirelessly, I spent about an hour with customer support before being informed of this limitation on the extender. The product listing says "compatible with all Wi-Fi routers," and it may be compatible with all routers if set up as a wired extender, but apparently it isn't compatible with all as a wirelessly connected extender. If you want wireless connection to your router, check your router's capability and make sure it is a dual-band router before ordering.

As I mentioned, I did get it set up as a wire-connected extender using an ethernet cable. And it works well for that. It puts a good strong WiFi signal all over our house and much of the yard. I'm giving it four stars for that.
text_fidelity_b: Linksys WiFi Extender, WiFi 6 Range Booster, Dual-Band Booster, Internet Repeater, 2,000 Sq. ft Coverage, Speeds up to (AX1800) 1.8Gbps - RE7310

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Washable Wired Keyboard K310 I often eat at my desk, which is not the greatest thing. Croissant flakes, bits of cheese and even rice grains often find their way into the crevices of my standard keyboard at work. It gets really disgusting. A few times crumbs got stuck inside the keys and stopped them from working properly. I've used compressed air cans and mini vaccuums but they don't do that great a job. I often end up having to flip the thing over and give it a shake. In addition, I remove all the keys and use a Q-tip to wipe up dust and dirt that get encrusted in these tiny spaces, which is time-consuming.

So you can tell I was relieved to get this washable keyboard. This thing is made for the Oscar Madisons of the world (like me). While you can't use it underwater while scuba diving (the instructions say you shouldn't submerge it in more than 11" of water, and no more than 5 minutes at that), being able to do a wash and rinse (as if it were a dinner plate) is more than enough to get most dirt and crumbs out.

I also like the fact that there is no additional software to install - just plug into the standard USB port, wait a few minutes until your computer recognizes the hardware, and then you're off. The keyboard is about the same size as other computer keyboards, except that the keys feel more like ones you'd find on a laptop. They are round and smooth and make me feel I'm pushing buttons. Because they lay flatter on the surface of the keyboard, you get a softer sound when you type as opposed to the hardier tapping of regular keyboards.

It took me awhile to get used to the feel. The buttons lack the slightly concave ridges that keep your fingers nestled so my fingers felt slippery on them, but not enough to have a problem.

Despite these reservations, however, I think this is a well-made product that is very practical, especially for people like me, who'd rather write than clean. Now all I need is a washable mouse!
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Washable Wired Keyboard K310

text_fidelity_a: Fitbit Flex Wireless Activity + Sleep Wristband, Slate, Small/Large If you hate the thought of wasting money on something that will just end up falling off your wrist, then DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT. I purchased two Fitbit Flex models, one for myself and one for my husband, on April 30, 2015. I didn't buy them from Amazon, but I did buy them from an authorized retailer. By October, my husband had quit wearing his because it wouldn't sync (we figured out this was easily fixed by restarting the phone the Fitbit app was installed on). He put his up and I continued wearing mine. During this time, my Fitbit started unlatching and falling off my wrist occasionally. I would find it laying around, or would notice, then retrace my steps and find the tracker. Fast forward to January: my Fitbit tracker fell off and was lost for good. I couldn't find it anywhere. I assume some lucky soul found it and calls it their own now. I started wearing my husband's tracker at this time with no issues. Then in March, it fell off my wrist in the parking lot of my office. I didn't notice this until it was too late. Someone I work with found it and returned it to me. Unfortunately, it was ran over by a vehicle (judging by the marks on the band) and crushed. No more Fitbit. Full disclosure: I tended to play with the fastener on my first Fitbit, though I made myself not do that anymore after losing it and using the second one. I also had 9 total bands with which I used the Fitbits in  this review. I though rotating between the bands daily would keep the fastenings tighter and reduce the risk of losing my Fitbit. Not so. When I decided to contact Fitbit and ask if they might be able to help me remain a loyal customer by giving me a percentage off my next Fitbit purchase, they obliged after a string of emails back and forth, sending me an email code to be used ONLY on their website. The discount was for 25% off, which is the everyday price on many of their items on Amazon. I should have pushed for more, but I didn't realize that until I went to compare their web prices with those on Amazon. In short, I feel like I dropped $200+ on Fitbit products and all of that money was lost. Their products with a watchband type fastener seem to be better, so my only caveat is that if you choose to buy the Flex, be prepared to lose it. I am currently without a tracker and have thought about buying one, but I am gun shy when it comes to dropping another $150 on a Fitbit Charge HR (has a watchband fastener) when I know the company doesn't stand behind their products. Sorry, Fitbit.

text_fidelity_a:
Fire HD 8 Tablet, 8" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB - Includes Special Offers, Magenta (Previous Generation - 5th) I got the HD 8 as a replacement to my old Kindle keyboard that died on a camp trip. I had such high hopes this device would fit the bill. I am not going to go into the nitty gritty of pros and cons but will sum up my experience highlights.

- the Audio performance is amazing. It is a quantum improvement from the audio I get on my iPad Mini. The sound experience is really something Apple should strive for. It did knock my socks off.

- setup was easy and efficient, but I think the OS and maybe even the device has problems. I have had to call tech support about twice a day on days I use the device. It is usually a lockup or hang or feature that does not work. I think I have isolated the problem to the fact the device can't keep the OS stable on battery. They always have me plug the device into the adapter for any support call (regardless of its charge level) and it always starts behaving itself once it is on DC power vs battery. I have also seen it burn through battery pretty fast at times. Not sure what it is doing but it ate 10% sitting on standby in my pack on the commute to work this morning!

- I do think the read aloud smarts have been improved since the older model (kbd) as it reads much cleaner now for me. (Less stops, more in the right locations, etc).

My end-game is that I will probably return it. If it does not work reliably on battery then it is not a mobile device. Period.
text_fidelity_b: Fire HD 8 Tablet, 8" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB - Includes Special Offers, Magenta (Previous Generation - 5th)

text_fidelity_a: Lenovo Chromebook C330 2-in-1 Convertible Laptop, 11.6" HD Display, MediaTek MT8173C, 4GB RAM, 64GB Storage, Chrome OS, Blizzard White Chromebook prices range from around $100 to over $1000. Better Chromebooks have Intel Core CPUs for great performance. The much cheaper Mediatek system in this Chromebook gives it mediocre performance, especially for intensive games or for business users who open lots of tabs simultaneously and frequently switch between them. On the plus side this Chromebook has a useful 4GB of RAM, a sharp colorful IPS screen, a touch screen that works great with Android apps, a very responsive (for swiping) touchpad, and reliable WiFi (much better than my HP laptop). On the minus side, the white plastic shell looks and feels a little cheap, the screen is not very bright, and the touchpad's button feels a little clunky. In summary, if you can't afford more than $300, this is a good choice for casual users who only have a few tabs open at once and use it mostly for email, Facebook, web surfing, and streaming music or videos. If you can afford $350 to $400, you will have several choices with more powerful CPUs for more intensive users.
text_fidelity_b: Lenovo Chromebook C330 2-in-1 Convertible Laptop, 11.6" HD Display, MediaTek MT8173C, 4GB RAM, 64GB Storage, Chrome OS, Blizzard White

Aside from its designed task, it does give you access to extra USB ports. There are 4 ports and only 2 are being used. It is very easy for me to reach across my desktop and plug in a device to charge, or plug in a thumb drive to save a file instead of reaching underneath the desk on my hands and knees. I love this product and the price is right. No need in my opinion to pay more.

EDIT: I have changed rating from 5 starts to 2 stars. The switch just died after 9 months of use. There is power going to both sides of the switch, but no data going back to the computer. I emailed customer service 2 times during the past week and have not gotten a response. Maybe they are off for Christmas? I don't now what they do in China. I have been happy with all the Ugreen products I have used and it's possible this may be a fluke. If the company continues to ignore my emails I will probably purchase a device from a different manufacturer. I am a little annoyed.

The largest screen in the iPad series makes multi-tasking possible, but the Apple Pencil goes right to the heart of iOS and the iPad Pro, touch. Yes, it is not your finger, but it enables pointing and drawing accurately.

My experience using a demo Apple Pencil and iPad Pro in an Apple Store enabled me to make a decision immediately. No buttons on this mouse, it is simple and intuitive. The point is firm, not squishy like all other styli I have used.

I placed an order online with the Apple Store and was prepared to wait 4-5 weeks to take delivery. The very next day I visited my University Bookstore where 20 were in stock.

I use the Pencil now successfully for note taking using the iOS Notes App and use Paper by 53 for drawing.

Don't hesitate. Buy an iPad Pro now. You will not look back.

text_fidelity_a: Vanstarry Beginners Microscope Kit 40X-1000X for Kids & Students, Dual LED Lights and Cordless Capability, Illumination Lab Compound Monocular Microscopes with Optical Glass Lenses & 12 Slides This is just what I used to use in the lab and I feel very thankful to be able to own one because they used to be thousands of dollars. This is more of a middle school /high school lab microscope, definitely not for kids but yes you can use it as beginner, just that I'm not sure about your definition of beginner because I'm not letting my toddler touch anything. It's of good weight, easy to adjust, two lens for viewing through eyes or phone, came with some sample specimens to look at and a manual that there's a lot of reading. Specimens are in glass like how you used to get in the lab, also came with blank ones that you can make your own (like swabbing your mouth). First off you do have to check all the lenses because they can be loose. Mine were and I caught it, glad nothing broke. I personally didn't feel it easy to understand the instructions so I'd say it's better if you have experience in the past (or YouTube) so touching a delicate equipment like this isn't as intimidating. Now I couldn't get the cell phone feature to work. It uses suction cups and my phone keeps sliding down with gravity. When I try to look with my phone it's the best I could get(in the picture) . Because of that I say this microscope failed my cell phone test, but everything else works as described.

text_fidelity_a:
Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I have been using the Kindle for exactly one week and it has exceeded my expectations in every way except for one design flaw.

Downloading books is absolutely a breeze and the selection of titles (for a premier launch of a product) is simply outstanding. I cannot wait to see what else will be added in the future and my credit card is ready and waiting.

Figuring out how to use the Kindle was easier than figuring out my basic LG cellphone. I am, obviously, a technical loser, but the Kindle has made me feel like a genius. And the instruction manual makes everything logical and simple to do - layed out for the quickest access. You don't feel intimidated or stupid when attempting to look something up.

My only complaint is that I wish there were some way of locking the right side "turn page" function. Unfortunately I have had to learn to grab my Kindle from the top and bottom because if I handle it from the sides, I will end up rapidly changing pages. And I know better than to lean it against anything on the right or left side for the same reason.

This the best Christmas gift I could have hoped for. I am now in the process of reading 6 different books, with 2 more in the queue. Not to mention 3 blogs which I check throughout the day.

The Kindle has opened up new worlds for me and is giving me the opportunity to discover subjects that I would never have considered in a million years. And why not? Instead of stacking books throughout my house, I can now carry them around in a compact unit which is lighter than a paperback.

I don't know who to thank for this wonderful creation, but I can assure you that I will be a customer for life.
text_fidelity_b: Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

text_fidelity_a:
Pioneer Elite SP-EC73 Andrew Jones Home Audio Center Channel Speaker Atmos is the newest (at least at the time of this writing) innovation from Dolby. The idea is, rather than discrete speakers, the system packages sound into objects and has the speakers work together to play the sounds in the way that most recreates what is intended. So in theory you can have as many speakers as you want. In practice, the receivers will support but so many and people will want but so many in their living room. Speakers will always need to have some distance between them or the sounds will blur. The format allows for sound from all directions, including the ceiling and not many people are going to want to hang speakers from the ceiling, which is where a speaker like this comes in.

It has two input pairs, top and bottom. DO NOT plug in the top pair unless your receiver supports Atmos. You can damage it that way. If it does, you put the "upper" speakers into the top pair and these speakers fire upward to bounce the sound off the ceiling giving you the illusion of sound from above.

If you don't yet have Atmos, and you want to pick up great speakers now, and build up over time, you can totally do that with these. You plug in the bottom pair (these will be connected even with Atmos) and let them sit in any speaker position in your configuration. They work well in any standard configuration.

The sound quality is crisp and clear and the range in both pitch and volume is remarkable. The footprint is much smaller than the photo had led me to believe. It looks like an elegant piece of furniture. I love it.

You will need a Philips head screwdriver to put on the base. There are spikes to help balance it on a carpet, but mine lives on a hardwood floor, so I did not attach those.
text_fidelity_b: Pioneer Elite SP-EC73 Andrew Jones Home Audio Center Channel Speaker

Sony XBR75Z9F 75-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart BRAVIA LED TV I really need to begin this review by stating that I am not much of a television watcher - up until this beast was delivered to me a few days ago, and I wanted to sit and experience it before I weighed in. There is not going to be a whole bunch of technical spiel simply because I don't know much about the mighty specs that make this thing cost a fortune, however, when I sit in front of it, I am TRANSFIXED.

I have to tear myself away from the stunning visuals, of which I tested from the mundane to my absolute favorites: regular television shows to the ones that make this a movie theater in your home - watching American Beauty WITH the commentary on so I can be ensorcelled by the teachable moments in cinematography, geeking out on Planet Earth, almost feeling the waves of water, the majestic mountains at your lap, the vivid plumage and wrinkles of parrots and elephants. The elegant clouds soaring through the sky, the dust whirling around in the desert. I am just blown away by how much these images are brought to life with the 4K HD capabilities, and for a TV at this price point the sound BETTER be amazing, which it is. Netflix and Chill will never be the same.

I come home, turn this thing on and feel like Red when he is gliding across the water to meet his dear Andy Dufresne in Shawshank Redemption. I feel like Shug Avery when her father finally welcomes her into the church with open arms. LOL!

There are smart TVs and in this case, this is a genius - once you take it out of the cocoon of careful packaging and set it up, all you have to do is enjoy your apps and Smart Home features like Alexa. Screen mirroring means you can play media right from your phone. Add the Firestick and access any show pretty much from the beginning of time. HDMI connection is a breeze. Football fans will be BLOWN AWAY by the picture quality too, as with any sport.

I don't have anything bad to say - only that I am sad that this thing is SO expensive. So to that end, WATCH OUT for generous discounts as the holidays approach. And even on sale, this TV is so damn incredible that you simply won't have to buy another one for years. Put that way, this is worth three dollars a day over the course of those years for something you will not ever experience elsewhere from Sony's top of the line. This Master's series is truly masterful.

I was fortunate enough in that this model worked perfectly for me right out of the box and was astonished to read about the other viewer's experience, and do hope that this review of a WORKING model will help. I'm looking at the cheaper Sony models for a television for my bedroom and will be watching those sales myself. I'm so thankful to have been able to receive this because I am turned on AND plugged in in a way that I really had no idea was possible!

ETUCRAY Headphone Jack Adapter for Phone Dongle Aux Audio to 3.5mm Cables Earphone Adaptor Headset Splitter for Music&Charger This is a very easy to use timer with some features that I’ve not come across before. It offers three main modes:

1) Clock – standard digital clock
2) Count up timer – can count up from zero to time events. It counts in whole seconds, so it’s not a true stopwatch.
3) Count down timer - you can set it to count down to zero.

The three modes are set by a sliding switch on the left so it’s very easy to change between the modes. It also has a memory feature so you can store a value and re-use it. For example, I use the count down feature to time tea brews, and have set a value of 3 min into memory. To repeat the countdown all I have to do is press the memory button and it sets itself to 3 min.

The best feature is that you can turn off the beep! There are three notification methods: a standard beep, vibrate or a flashing red LED. That’s a huge plus since I usually carry the timer with me and find the beep to be very annoying. The light or vibrate options are far nicer to use. I would imagine the flashing LED light option would be especially appreciated by the hearing impaired. You set the notification type with a switch on the back.

The overall build quality feels very solid. The numbers are large (about 0.75 inches tall) and easy to read even though the screen is not backlit. There a clip on the back that includes a magnet, so you can position this on a fridge or stove hood. The clip does not detach, but the profile is low enough that it doesn’t cause a problem if you want to carry the timer in your pocket.

It runs on 1 AAA battery (included). The package is easy to open – no clamshell to have to wrestle with.

It’s a well-made timer with some great convenience features built in. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: ETUCRAY Headphone Jack Adapter for Phone Dongle Aux Audio to 3.5mm Cables Earphone Adaptor Headset Splitter for Music&Charger

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm X-E2 16.3 MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 3.0-Inch LCD - Body Only (Silver) I've been thinking about upgrading from my Canon 50d for awhile now. I thought I wanted a full frame camera, but I could never justify spending that kind of money on a hobby. One of the main reasons was that I had sort of got out of the habit of shooting as much as I used. Part of the reason was that it always seemed like such a pain to lug around the camera. There were always times I wish I had a camera, but didn't.

This camera solves a lot of that for me. Take the lens off the body and the thing literally fits in your pocket. Leave it on and it fits nicely in my car's center console. It feels nice in my hands, although I bought the metal thumb grip at the same time as the camera and must admit that does help quite a bit.

Compared to my 50d (which is a little long in the tooth) the image quality is superior. The color reproduction in particular seemed to be good. It also seemed to perform better at higher ISOs than my 50d does. Really, the only area where the 50d still out-performs the XE-2 is how fast the autofocus works. The XE-2 is good, but my 50d is still a touch better. Maybe a firmware update will improve this.

Despite using a Canon products for almost a decade, I found I really like the controls on this camera. I found it really easy and intuitive to change the shutter speed and aperature. ISO and most of the other frequently used settings are easily reached by hitting the Q button. The layout could be tweaked a little, but overall it's pretty good.

I've never had a camera with wifi, but it's a feature that's gotten more use than I thought it would. Being able to transmit pictures to Facebook, Twitter, or whatever is really simple once you upload the photo from the camera using Fuji's app. I don't post a lot of pictures online, but that may change a little bit now that it is a lot simpler.

The build quality is really good and the included kit lens is really nice. The screen is sharp and the EVF is clear. Like I mentioned before, the size of the frame is nice and compact and is much easier to take along wherever you go.

Is this a replacement for a full frame DSLR? No. Is it a good alternative for a crop sensor DSLR? In my opinion, absolutely. First, the price and performance makes it very competitive. Second, the size is going to be tough to beat. Finally, for me at least, it is a camera I am more likely to use more and take with me more places. As other's have mentioned about this camera though, if you like putting everything on automatic or different shooting modes (sports, portrait, landscape, etc) then this camera is probably not for you. If you are interested in learning how to shoot without those crutches, this camera would be a great place to start.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm X-E2 16.3 MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 3.0-Inch LCD - Body Only (Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
Roku Express - HD Streaming Player It may not be a techie's delight, but if you are looking for a budget streaming device, this one fits the bill. First off it is quite small making it ideal for cramped or limited spaces like a vacation home or boat. It comes with a short, two foot long cable and a piece of two sided tape. It connects to your tv with the cable.Depending where you tv is located you might have to use a longer cable. I did and found that the tape is not just a nice idea, it is a necessity. the box is so small and most cables so rigid it flips the box off making it impossible to regulate with the infrared remote. Take time to position because while the tape adheres well it looses its stickiness after being removed and repositioned. The infrared remote must be in line of sight for it to work. The way around that is to use the app. The app works with both android and iOS. The app has a voice control which I found to be inconsistent and a private listening feature that lets you use your phone headphones and mute the TV.

Performance is mixed. navigating and launching is slow. Netflix in particular really dragged. but playing content was excellent with no lag or problems. the channel selection is good with pretty much everything you would want available.

This is not bad for a budget streamer. there are definitely downsides, the ir remote, the lack of speed, the need for a cable. but it does work and is small enough for travel. I am frequently on the road for business and this does expand the limited options of hotel televisions. If you are on a budget and don't need or want the features that are available on pricier models this low end streamer will get the job done.
text_fidelity_b: Roku Express - HD Streaming Player

Skullcandy Hesh ANC Wireless Over-Ear Noise Cancelling Bluetooth Headphones for iPhone and Android with Microphone / 22 Hour Battery Life / Best for Music, School, Workouts, Travel, and Gaming - White Skullcandy’s description says it all: wireless simplicity with noise canceling. These aren’t headphones for audiophiles who want to control and customize every sound option. These are headphones for people who want affordable Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) and decent sound output.

I’ve noticed the ANC works better when I’m listening to music rather than if I’m watching a tv show or movie to cancel out the background noise in my home. If I am watching a show, I can hear someone else watching a video in the next room; the noise of their video is cut about 75-80%. If I have music on, the noise of their video is cut about 90-100%, depending on the type of music.

Switching ANC on and off is easy. The headphones have a dedicated button for that, one second press to turn on, one second press to turn off. So it’s very quick if I need to hear someone speaking. The button has a raised open circle (◯) on it, so once you get used to the different symbols on the buttons, it’s very easy to feel it. The headphones also provide audio indicators (“Noise cancelling off/on”) when turning the ANC on and off.

The other buttons include + for volume up/track forward, ⚫ for power/play/pause, and -- for volume down/track back. I’ve used Skullcandy headphones for years when working outside, and I really like that they keep using physical buttons. I find physical buttons so much easier to use and know what button I’m pressing.

Sound quality is okay. I’ve noticed that the bass seems punchy, like I can feel it echoing against my ears. I don’t often mess with sound profiles, but this is a case where I would try to reduce the bass for my audio comfort. Otherwise, the sound is average to good.

The headphones stayed in place on my head, from sitting at my desk to walking around the house, folding laundry, and putting it away. I didn’t try with intensive activity, but as I mentioned above, I’ve used the previous versions of Skullcandy Hesh for working outside and they stay put. These look and feel almost identical to my old Hesh headphones, so I’m confident these will perform the same. They are tight; I sometimes get a headache when wearing them.

The headphones charge via USB-C. The box includes a USB cable and an audio cable. I used the headphones for about a week, probably 20 hours, before needing to charge. I like that I can get 3 hours of use with a 10 minute charge, very handy for if I’m going somewhere and forgot to charge ahead of time.
text_fidelity_b: Skullcandy Hesh ANC Wireless Over-Ear Noise Cancelling Bluetooth Headphones for iPhone and Android with Microphone / 22 Hour Battery Life / Best for Music, School, Workouts, Travel, and Gaming - White
