text_fidelity_a:
RUBAN Notebook Lock and Security Cable (PC/Laptop) Two Keys 6.6 Foot (Black) This notebook lock and security cable works with laptops that have a Kensington security slot (about 99% of them on the market do), so it will work for most notebooks except the MacBook Pro. Be sure to check to make sure your laptop has the security port which looks like a small slot usually found in the upper right outside corner.

To use this cable run the end of the cable around a fixed object that can't be moved without effort or drawing attention, such as the leg of a heavy table or a post, then loop the locking end through the loop and attach it to your laptop. The locking mechanism has a built in bar that fits into the Kensington slot, so just insert it into the port, then turn the key 90 degrees to lock it in place. You'll need the key to unlock it when you're ready to take the laptop so be sure to bring it along. When you want to remove your laptop just rotate the key in the opposite direction to unlock it. This set comes with a spare key as well in case you misplace one.

The cable that comes with this is 6.2" long which wasn't long enough to go over the top of my desk and come back up to secure my laptop to the desk that way, but it was adequate to secure it around one of the desk's legs, so this cable isn't intended to permanently affix your laptop to a desk top, and it's thin enough to cut with bold cutters, but it's long enough and strong enough to deter someone from being able to snatch and run off with your laptop when you're at the library or coffee shop and want to leave it unattended long enough to go use the copy machine or go get a refill!

I like how the T-bar mechanism works to secure the lock to the laptop but still allow complete cable movement and rotation without dislodging the lock from the laptop, and I also like the fact that the cable is coated to prevent damage to your laptop & whatever the cable is secured around. This laptop lock and security cable is going to be perfect for my daughter when she studies in the campus library.

I received this notebook lock and security cable for testing and review. It works a lot easier than I expected!
text_fidelity_b: RUBAN Notebook Lock and Security Cable (PC/Laptop) Two Keys 6.6 Foot (Black)

text_fidelity_a: Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st) The new Kindle arrived within 2 days of my order. I sat down and played around with it for a few minutes and learned the icons but that's all that can be done until it is registered with Amazon. I took it to Toyota while getting my car serviced. Our local Toyota dealer has free WiFi for customers. The Kindle found the hot spot and Amazon recognized the Kindle right away.  It took a few taps around the screen to get started but was easy with a little exploring. Within the time to get an oil change, I had downloaded my ebooks from Cloud and even bought a nice app on sale.  Next I stopped by BestBuy and added a Kindle micro USB to USB cable.  The cable can be used to download ebooks from your PC when not connected to wireless.  Using free Calibre to manage the free ebooks from the Internet, enables covers and metadata for those ebooks that have none.  Calibre will also download the books to Kindle from a PC.  The Fire is great but took some thinking and patience to get it to do all the things I imagined it would do. For instance, ebooks without covers will all look alike and have no title.  This is why it is important to use Calibre for ebook management. Reading ebooks is so much better than it was 10 years ago and this is only the beginning.  The download speed is great.  The reading speed is also great.The storage space is really more than enough.  The 8 Gigabytes of memory is close to 2 warehouses of data.  I read that somewhere on Wikipedia in the middle of the night.  To put it in proportion, imagine having up to 6000 books in your home. The Kindle does not get hot like a netbook and is smaller and lighter too.  The battery life is much better than my 7" netbook also.  Like other customers, I would have liked the micro USB to USB cable included in the box.  3G would be great too.  The best thing about Kindle Fire is the color.  The color is as beautiful as everyone says it is.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st)

text_fidelity_a:
VideoSecu 2 Heavy Duty PA DJ Club Adjustable Height Satellite Speaker Stand Mount - Extends 26.5" to 47" (i.e. Bose, Harmon Kardon, JBL, KEF, Klipsch, Sony, Yamaha, Pioneer and Others) 1B7 These are very flimsy stands. They may be ok with small speakers (e.g. small bookshelf speakers or monitors with 4" woofers) when set to the shortest possible height, but I wouldn't even think of putting a PA speaker on one of these. The dimensions of the base is 8" x 8". Unless you are planning to bolt them to the ground, you definitely don't want to put a speaker cabinet that is heavier than 10lbs or wider than 6" on one of these. Because of the single (and small diameter) pole design, stability is very poor, no matter what how much you tighten the screws or center-balance your speakers. The side arms that are supposed to cradle the bottoms of the speakers from the sides is a mechanically poor design. The platform that the speaker sits on is only 4" deep. Given that a lot of monitor speakers are deep and the weight is distributed in the front (woofer) and back (plate amplifier), front-back wobble will be nearly impossible to eliminate.

The only way to use these speaker stands in a safe way for 5.25" or 6.25" bookshelf speakers would be to bolt the bottom plates on a sturdy piece of wood or MDF that is at least 12"x12".
text_fidelity_b: VideoSecu 2 Heavy Duty PA DJ Club Adjustable Height Satellite Speaker Stand Mount - Extends 26.5" to 47" (i.e. Bose, Harmon Kardon, JBL, KEF, Klipsch, Sony, Yamaha, Pioneer and Others) 1B7

text_fidelity_a:
Motorola T200TP Talkabout Radio, 3 Pack GMRS walkie-talkies like this have been around for decades. Unfortunately, the technology hasn't really improved in all that time. The specs that are listed in the description are greatly exaggerated. We only get 4-5 hours of moderate use from the rechargeable batteries. Fortunately, you can replace them with fresh AA batteries in the field to extend your usage time. The 20 mile range is really a hoax. Even the most optimal situation when one of us is on top of a hill and the others are visible in the valley below, we've never gotten more than 10 miles. In clear flat situations like across a lake or a farm field, range is a 3-4 miles at best. In a forest or city where there are lots of obstructions, range can be less than 1 mile.

20 years ago, few people had cell phones so these radios were really popular. Not so much anymore. That means you get much less interference on each channel. We find the radios useful for family outings since the kids don't have cell phones and many of the parks we visit have terrible cell phone coverage.

The radios are fairly lightweight (about 6 ounces each including the batteries). The package includes 3 battery packs and 2 chargers. One of the chargers has a splitter so it can charge 2 radios at the same time. You can also use your micro-USB cell phone charger to charge the radios. You can also use your own rechargeable AA batteries with your own charger. Replacing the batteries is kind of a hassle since the belt clip blocks the battery cover, though I suppose that also helps keep the battery cover in place. No carrying cases or storage case is included, through the radios are pretty durable and the shipping box works well for storage.

Note that USA use requires a Federal FCC radio license. The photo here is from the instruction manual. Many (perhaps most) users violate Federal law and use them without license, but who knows what enforcement will be like in the future. Other countries have stricter laws and I have heard about some tourists getting into trouble using radios like this.
text_fidelity_b: Motorola T200TP Talkabout Radio, 3 Pack

text_fidelity_a:
Sony Walkman NWZA17SLV 64 GB Hi-Res Digital Music Player (Silver) I am writing this review because after reading the few reviews available it sounded like this would be a great Media Player. But after receiving the player (a Christmas gift from my wife) I have to wonder if most of the people who reviewed the unit have actually used or even seen one in person. So I reread the reviews and noticed a trend that they don't actually say anything about using the player (all except one).
So here is a real user review.
The good. (I use it for music playback only)
The sound on the player is superb. I rip my cd's using the FLAC format and I have listed to playback using Wired (Grado's) and Bluetooth headphones. I have also listened to it on my home stereo using wired and a Bluetooth connection. There is a slight difference in the tonal quality but in a noisy environment my ears can't tell the difference. Sony digital processor does seem to color the music a little but it is on the warm side so it not objectionable.
I must say I love the sound of this player.
The media program (Media Go) that comes with it is very good for ripping music in any format that the player supports. Setting up playlist to send to the player is a breeze. The program does not have the options of JRiver Media Center but it is simpler to use.
The Bad
It is cheaply built - If feels like a toy. I do not believe it will stand up to daily use. Not a quality product that I have come to expect from Sony. For the price of this unit I expect it to at least have the build quality of my FiiO player or my cassette Walkman (which still works)
Bluetooth- It's a joke. My main reason of wanting this player was Bluetooth connectivity. If you disconnect it from the headphones, stereo -car and home, It take at least three tries for it to reconnect the next time you want to use it and you have to navigate to the Bluetooth screen to do it.
This creates a problem on its own. If you were listening to your playlist and stop at a particular track you now loose that place unless you navigate back to the home screen (more on that later) and bookmark your spot before you try and reconnect to your Bluetooth playback source. This is a major pain.
Screen Navigation. The player has 4 main buttons. The toggle button which surrounds the play and pause button is use for navigation. The navigation is more cumbersome -not user friendly- than it needs to be. Try and navigate while you are working out or somewhere not so well lit and it is frustrating at best. At this price it should have a touch screen. My 29 dollar SanDisk player is easier to use that this setup.
The next problem. You really can't power down the player. Once you power down the player if you accidently touch any button on the player it powers back up. I keep the player in a soft case clipped to my belt. I have bumped the player while in the case and have ended up with a dead battery the next time I wanted to use it.
There are other problems but they are minor and I can live with those.
If Sony wants to play in this market (no pun intended) these major flaws need to be fixed.
Tried to post a review on Sony's web site and they would not let it post. So I don't trust any reviews on their web site at this point. This is why I am posting it here to at least let potential buyers be aware of what it is really like to use this player.
text_fidelity_b: Sony Walkman NWZA17SLV 64 GB Hi-Res Digital Music Player (Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
JVC HARX700 Precision Sound Full Size Headphones - Black ~Comfortable for hours. These are light years ahead of earbuds, on ear, or over ear phones. No part of my ear was pinched or scrunched, even though I wear glasses. I have an over-sized melon and large, flat ears. I can't tolerate buds for more than about 30 minutes, and most headphones in this range are pinchy somewhere.
~I normally watch movies/videos at full sound with Closed Caption on iPad or laptops. I'm at half volume -- no CC -- wearing these phones. I was able to easily pick up male and female voices, including foreign accents.
~NOT noise cancelling. I could still hear the whir of a fan, my kids talking, etc., but they couldn't hear any noise coming from my headphones. For me, this was ideal. I don't have the luxury of tuning out the world most of the time.
~Requires several hours of break-in. I usually listen to Winterspell from Two Steps to test buds and phones. It sounded tinny on first listen, and amazing about 10 hours in.
I highly recommend these if you have moderate hearing loss. I can't differentiate consonant sounds, and certain voices and accents are nearly impossible for me to follow on screen. These didn't feel loud, just incredibly clear -- it was like hearing like a kid again.
text_fidelity_b: JVC HARX700 Precision Sound Full Size Headphones - Black
